title: Oceans and continents have kept roughly their present positions since the Silurian

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Oceans and continents have kept roughly their present positions since the Silurian

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Since no oceanic island bears Palaeozoic or Secondary formations, oceans have probably occupied their present areas, and continents theirs, since the earliest Silurian period, though the arrangement may have differed long before.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On the Imperfection of the Geological Record

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: we may infer that where our oceans now extend, oceans have extended from the remotest period of which we have any record; and on the other hand, that where continents now exist, large tracts of land have existed, subjected no doubt to great oscillations of level, since the earliest silurian period.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter IX, “On the Imperfection of the Geological Record”; section “On their sudden appearance in the lowest known fossiliferous strata”. Scope: global distribution of oceans and continents since the Silurian

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch09-14: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.79

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Modern plate reconstructions make the spatial proposition explicit and strongly discriminating. Deep-time ocean-basin uncertainty remains, but existing data can clearly confirm or refute the broad stated inference.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct Silurian-to-present continental crust, ocean basins, and paleoshorelines from plate models and geological constraints. Quantify overlap between ancient and present continental and oceanic areas; extensive changes would refute rough positional continuity.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Published plate models directly record whether oceans and continents stayed in their present areas. The displacements involved, such as the opening of the Atlantic, are large relative to reconstruction uncertainty. Paleozoic detail is coarser, but it is still sufficient to confirm or refute stability since the earliest Silurian.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare Silurian-to-Recent paleogeographic reconstructions with the present positions of continents and ocean basins. Opening or closure of major ocean basins, or large lateral shifts of continental crust, would refute long-term stability of those areas.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Paleozoic plate reconstructions are less precise than Mesozoic and Cenozoic ones.

Ocean crust older than the Jurassic has been subducted, so ancient ocean positions are inferred from continental margins.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: If oceans have occupied their present areas and continents theirs since the earliest Silurian, then at every time from ~440 Ma to the present the geographic locations now occupied by land were occupied by continental land, and the locations now occupied by ocean were ocean.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: Coastline polygons of the MERDITH2021 plate model were downloaded from the GPlates Web Service at 0 Ma and at 440, 400, 350, 300, 250, 200, 150, 100 and 50 Ma, and rasterised by even-odd point-in-polygon onto a 2x2 degree grid (16,200 cells, cos-latitude weighted). Present land (28.8% of the globe, matching the real land fraction) was defined from the 0 Ma coastlines. For each past time the fraction of present land cells lying inside reconstructed coastlines (L_t) and of present ocean cells lying outside them (O_t) was computed, and L_all / O_all as the fractions persisting at all nine times. The same was run with the PALEOMAP model.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Using the GPlates Web Service with the Merdith et al. (2021) plate model, the model's coastline polygons are reconstructed to 440, 400, 350, 300, 250, 200, 150, 100 and 50 Ma. On a 2x2 degree global grid (area-weighted by cos latitude), classify each present-day grid cell as land or ocean from the time-0 coastlines. L_all = area fraction of present land cells that fall inside reconstructed coastline polygons at every one of the nine times; O_all = area fraction of present ocean cells that fall outside them at every time. The claim is SUPPORTED if L_all >= 0.75 and O_all >= 0.75.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. The claim is REFUTED if L_all < 0.50 or O_all < 0.50. Intermediate outcomes are 'mixed'. For comparison the per-time fractions (L_t, O_t) and the expected overlap for randomly placed continents (equal to the present land fraction) are reported. The PALEOMAP model is run as a robustness check and is not part of the verdict.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: area fraction of present-day land that lies within reconstructed continental coastlines at all nine times 440-50 Ma (MERDITH2021)

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: O_all (present ocean that was ocean at all times) = 0.3377; PALEOMAP robustness: L_all = 0.0046, O_all = 0.3436

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Darwin's 'where our oceans now extend, oceans have extended' and 'where continents now exist, large tracts of land have existed ... since the earliest silurian period' is read as spatial persistence of land and ocean in a fixed geographic (Earth) frame, which is how he and his contemporaries understood it (he explicitly allows 'great oscillations of level' but not lateral movement). Plate reconstructions place continental crust in a palaeomagnetic / mantle reference frame; the coastline polygons of the plate model are used as the outline of continental land at each time. Modern reinterpretation: the claim is tested against reconstructed continental positions, which did not exist as a concept in 1859; palaeolongitude in the Palaeozoic is uncertain, which could shift overlap either way.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value:
GPlates Web Service, reconstruct/coastlines with model MERDITH2021 (Merdith et al. 2021, Earth-Science Reviews 214:103477)

GPlates Web Service, reconstruct/coastlines with model PALEOMAP (Scotese PALEOMAP PaleoAtlas)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
At 440 Ma only 22% of present land area lay under reconstructed continental land at the same geographic location, less than the 29% expected if continents were placed at random, and 78% of present ocean area was ocean, close to the random expectation of 71%; essentially no present land (0.07%) was land continuously at all nine times, and only 34% of present ocean was ocean throughout (the Pacific). PALEOMAP gives the same picture (0.5% and 34%).

Plate models place continents in a palaeomagnetic or mantle reference frame; palaeolongitude is poorly constrained in the Palaeozoic, so the exact overlap at 440-300 Ma is uncertain, but no reference-frame choice can keep the Atlantic and Indian Ocean basins (which opened after 200 Ma) in place, so the refutation does not depend on the deep-time frame.

The coastline polygons are present-day coastlines carried rigidly with their plates, not palaeo-shorelines; they approximate continental crust rather than emergent land, which if anything favours Darwin's 'large tracts of land' reading.

The 2 degree grid and even-odd test treat polygon edges coarsely; this affects the fractions at the percent level only.

Darwin's inference (no oceanic island bears Palaeozoic or Secondary formations) remains an accurate observation; it is the inference of fixed continents and oceans that modern plate reconstructions contradict.
